entry.title: Take Back the Night Walk Returns to Downtown Roseburg October 22
entry.summary: Take Back the Night returns to downtown Roseburg October 22 with a gathering at the Douglas County Courthouse and a walk supporting survivors of sexual violence. Peace at Home Advocacy Center is hosting the event, with free registration available.

entry.title: Oregon Health Plan Payments To Regional Healthcare Organizations Set To Increase In 2027
entry.summary: Oregon plans to increase payments to the regional organizations that coordinate healthcare for Oregon Health Plan members in 2027. The proposed rates average $627.68 per member each month and await federal approval.

entry.title: Bend Police Update Classroom Count, Outline Next Steps In Silver Rail Shooting Investigation
entry.summary: Bend police confirmed four adults and five children were in the classroom during the Silver Rail Elementary shooting. Investigators expected to finish evidence collection at the school Monday, while officers will increase their presence as students return to campuses Wednesday.

entry.title: DFPA Responds To Two Weekend Fires As Fire Season Restrictions Continue

entry.title: Three Arrested After Reported Drive-By Shooting Outside Roseburg Bi-Mart
entry.summary: Three men were arrested after a reported drive-by shooting outside Roseburg’s Bi-Mart on Oct. 16. Police said a bullet struck an occupied vehicle, but the woman inside was unharmed. Officers later located the suspects in Sutherlin and recovered a stolen firearm.

entry.title: Police Log: October 16 - October 18, 2026
entry.summary: Roseburg police reported 12 incidents from October 16-19, including a reported shooting in the Bi-Mart parking lot, warrant arrests, theft, harassment, prohibited camping, and a dog bite at Stewart Park.

entry.title: Roseburg Forecast Calls for Mild Weather Through Midweek, With Rain Possible This Weekend
entry.summary: Roseburg will see mild, mostly dry weather through midweek, with highs reaching 75 degrees Wednesday. Cooler temperatures are expected later in the week, with the possibility of the area's first measurable rainfall in nearly four weeks arriving this weekend.

entry.title: Douglas County Receives National Financial Reporting Award for 38th Consecutive Year
entry.summary: Douglas County has earned national recognition for excellence in financial reporting for the 38th consecutive year, recognizing its commitment to accuracy, transparency, and accountability in managing public funds.

entry.title: Roseburg High School To Host Free Fall Choir Concert October 20
entry.summary: Roseburg High School will host a free Fall Choir Concert October 20 at 6:30 p.m. in the Rose Theatre. The community is invited to enjoy an evening of student music and support the school’s choir program.

entry.title: Wildlife Safari’s Zoobilee Returns October 23-25 With Three Nights Of Halloween Fun
entry.summary: Wildlife Safari's annual Zoobilee returns October 23-25 in Winston with three nights of trick-or-treating, a haunted house, costumes, and family-friendly Halloween activities from 5 to 8 p.m.

entry.title: Make a Difference Day Returns for Fifth Year With 15 Volunteer Projects Across Douglas County
entry.summary: Douglas County's fifth annual Make a Difference Day returns Saturday, October 24, with 15 volunteer projects supporting local schools, nonprofits, veterans, housing efforts, and environmental restoration. The event runs from 9 a.m. to noon.

entry.title: West Goedeck Avenue Closure Extended Through October 26
entry.summary: The closure of West Goedeck Avenue in Roseburg has been extended through 5 p.m. Monday, October 26, as crews continue sanitary sewer work. Motorists are advised to use alternate routes and allow extra travel time.

entry.title: Umpqua National Forest Offering Free Christmas Tree Cutting Permits for 2026
entry.summary: Christmas tree cutting permits are free on the Umpqua National Forest for 2026. Residents can cut up to four trees per household between October 19 and December 31. District maps and cutting guidelines are available online.

entry.title: Douglas County Voters Can Expect Ballots Soon for November 3 Election
entry.summary: Douglas County voters should begin receiving ballots soon for the November 3 election. County Clerk Dan Loomis reminds residents to check their mailboxes, sign their return envelopes, and return ballots by the deadline.

entry.title: Umpqua National Forest Announces Winter Campground Closures, With Several Sites Remaining Open Year-Round
entry.summary: The Umpqua National Forest has announced its tentative winter campground closure schedule. Several campgrounds will remain open year-round, while others are closing in late October or as snowfall arrives.

entry.title: Oregon Flags Lowered to Half-Staff Friday in Honor of Bend School Shooting Victims
